revised_comments: Côte d'Ivoire has a comprehensive strategic framework for government data exchange and interoperability. The National Digital Development Strategy 2021-2025, led by the Ministry of Digital Transition and Digitalisation, is organised around seven pillars including digital infrastructure, digital services and e-governance, and is reinforced by the 'Digital Acceleration Zero Paper 2030' plan with an associated $600 million investment programme. A dedicated interoperability roadmap adopted in 2022 underpins the data exchange agenda and culminated in the September 2025 launch of the UXP (Unified eXchange Platform), built by Estonia's Cybernetica and implemented by the Société Nationale de Développement Informatique (SNDI), which is piloted across 12 public institutions including the tax directorate, ONECI civil registration and the Abidjan Commercial Court, with wider rollout targeted by 2027. Digitalisation and interoperability are also positioned as central pillars of the Côte d'Ivoire 2030 Strategic Plan.
